results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** A probability-preserving system $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P,T)$ and finite-valued measurable functions $g_j\ge0$ with $g_j\to g$ almost surely and $G:=\sup_jg_j\in L^1(P)$.

[F1] [[thm-birkhoff-ergodic-theorem]]: time averages of an integrable function in a measure-preserving system converge almost surely to an integrable limit.

[F2] [[lem-ergodic-averages-converge-in-l-p-on-finite-measure-spaces]]: on a finite-measure space, the time averages converge in $L^1$ to their Birkhoff limit.

[F3] [[def-measure-preserving-transformation-and-system]]: $P(T^{-1}E)=P(E)$, so every $T^i$ preserves $P$.

[F4] [[thm-dominated-convergence]]: pointwise convergence under an integrable envelope implies convergence of integrals.



**Given:** The hypotheses and [F1]–[F4].

1.1 For each $K$, put $U_K=\sup_{j\ge K}|g_j-g|$. Then $U_K\downarrow0$ almost surely and $0\le U_K\le 2G$ almost surely, since $g\le G$ as a pointwise limit. Dominated convergence [F4] gives $\mathbb E U_K\to0$. [F4, given, algebra]

1.2 Since $g_i\to g$ almost surely and $|g_i-g|\le2G$, [F4] gives $E|g_i-g|\to0$. By stationarity [F3], $E|g_i-g|(T^i)=E|g_i-g|$, so the expectation of the absolute triangular error is $n^{-1}\sum_{i<n}E|g_i-g|\to0$ by Cesaro averaging. Thus the error tends to zero in $L^1$. [F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 Fix $K$. For $i\ge K$, $|g_i-g|\le U_K$. Hence for $n>K$, the average of $|g_i-g|\circ T^i$ is bounded by the first $K$ terms divided by $n$, plus $n^{-1}\sum_{i=K}^{n-1}U_K\circ T^i$. The first part tends to zero almost surely. By [F1], the second part converges almost surely to the Birkhoff limit $U_K^*$; by [F2], the averages converge to $U_K^*$ in $L^1$, so $E U_K^*=E U_K$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply step 2.1 to every integer $K$ on the intersection of the resulting countably many probability-one sets. The limsup of the left side is at most $U_K^*$ for each $K$. Since $U_K$ decreases pointwise, the averages and their limits $U_K^*$ decrease; their expectations equal $E U_K\to0$. Thus $\inf_KU_K^*=0$ almost surely, and the limsup is zero. Thus $n^{-1}\sum_{i<n}|g_i-g|(T^i\omega)\to0$ almost surely. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 By [F1]–[F2], the Birkhoff averages of $g$ converge almost surely and in $L^1$ to their Birkhoff limit. Steps 3.1 and 1.2 show the triangular averages differ from these averages by quantities tending to zero almost surely and in $L^1$, respectively. Hence both modes of convergence hold with the same limit. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

**Given:** Finite block laws $p_n$ on $\mathcal A^n$, entropy-rate candidate $h$, and normalized self-information $I_n(X^n)/n$ from [[def-finite-block-information-and-entropy]]. Assume $I_n(X^n)/n\to h$ in probability.

[F1] [[def-finite-block-information-and-entropy]]: $I_n(x)=-\log_2p_n(x)$ on positive-probability blocks.

[F2] [[def-finite-block-source-code]]: a rate-$R$ fixed-length code has at most $2^{\lfloor nR\rfloor}$ messages and success-set cardinality at most that number.



**Given:** The AEP convergence and finite-block coding convention [F1]–[F2].

1.1 Let $R>h$ and choose $\epsilon>0$ with $h+\epsilon<R$. Define $T_n=\{x:p_n(x)>0,\ I_n(x)\le n(h+\epsilon)\}$. On $T_n$, each word has probability at least $2^{-n(h+\epsilon)}$, so $|T_n|\le2^{n(h+\epsilon)}$. The AEP gives $P(X^n\in T_n)\to1$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 For all sufficiently large $n$, $|T_n|\le2^{\lfloor nR\rfloor}$. Assign distinct fixed-length messages to $T_n$ and decode all other messages as an arbitrary fixed word. The block error is at most $P(X^n\notin T_n)\to0$. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Let $R<h$ and choose $\epsilon>0$ with $R+\epsilon<h$. Any decoder succeeds on a set $S_n$ of at most $2^{\lfloor nR\rfloor}$ words. Split it according to whether $I_n(x)>n(R+\epsilon)$. The probability of successful words in that part is at most $2^{nR}2^{-n(R+\epsilon)}=2^{-n\epsilon}$, while the other part has total probability tending to zero by the AEP. Thus success probability tends to zero. At $R=h$ neither conclusion is asserted. [F1, F2, given, algebra] ∎

**Given:** A stationary finite-alphabet source $X$ with alphabet $\mathcal A$, and the finite-past probabilities and information variables $p_k,g_k$ of [[def-past-information-density-finite-alphabet]].

[F1] [[def-finite-alphabet-stationary-source]]: the shift preserves the path law.

[F2] [[def-past-information-density-finite-alphabet]]: $p_k(a)=P(X_0=a\mid X_{-k}^{-1})$ on finite atoms and $g_k=-\log_2p_k(X_0)$ almost surely.

[F3] [[lem-finite-block-entropy-chain-rule]]: block entropy is the sum of successive conditional entropies.

[F4] [[thm-stationary-entropy-rate-limit]]: $H(X_0^{n-1})/n$ converges to the entropy rate $h$.

[F5] [[thm-monotone-class]]: finite-past cylinder identities extend to the sigma-algebra they generate.



**Given:** The source and definitions [F1]–[F2].

1.1 For each $a\in\mathcal A$, $p_k(a)=E[1_{\{X_0=a\}}\mid\mathcal F_k]$ is a martingale in $k$ for $\mathcal F_k=\sigma(X_{-k},\ldots,X_{-1})$, because the finite-atom conditional averages satisfy the tower identity when the partition is refined. It is bounded between zero and one. [F2, given]

1.2 For rationals $0\le u<v\le1$, the usual buy-at-$u$, sell-at-$v$ strategy applied to this bounded martingale has expected gain zero; each completed upcrossing earns at least $v-u$, and an unfinished final holding loses at most one. Therefore the expected number of completed upcrossings by time $N$ is at most $(v-u)^{-1}$. Monotone convergence of the integer counts makes the total upcrossings finite almost surely. Intersect over the countably many rational pairs: each $p_k(a)$ then converges to some $p_\infty(a)\in[0,1]$. [F2, algebra]

1.3 For $t\ge0$, let $\tau$ be the first $k$ with $p_k(a)<2^{-t}$. On each event $\{\tau=k\}\in\mathcal F_k$, the tower identity gives $$P(X_0=a,\tau=k)=E[1_{\{\tau=k\}}p_k(a)]\le2^{-t}P(\tau=k).$$ Summing $k$ and then $a$ proves $P(\sup_k g_k>t)\le |\mathcal A|2^{-t}$. Thus $G=\sup_k g_k$ is integrable, and dominated convergence gives $E g_k\to E g_\infty$. [F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The limit is positive at the realized symbol almost surely. Indeed, for each $a$, $p_\infty(a)=E[1_{\{X_0=a\}}\mid\sigma(\cup_k\mathcal F_k)]$ by testing the limit on finite-past cylinders and [F5]; hence $P(X_0=a,p_\infty(a)=0)=E[1_{\{p_\infty(a)=0\}}p_\infty(a)]=0$. Summing over finite $\mathcal A$ gives $g_k\to g_\infty:=-\log_2p_\infty(X_0)<\infty$ almost surely. [F2, F5, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 By stationarity, [F3] gives $H_n=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}E g_k$. Cesàro convergence and [F4] yield $E g_\infty=\lim_nH_n/n=h$. This also covers zero-probability transitions because they are never observed. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.3, algebra] ∎
